29875-dreamers-of-the-ghetto.title: Dreamers Of The Ghetto
29875-dreamers-of-the-ghetto.creator: Unknown
29875-dreamers-of-the-ghetto.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In dream I saw two Jews that met by chance,  One old, stern-eyed, deep-browed, yet garlanded  With living light of love around his head,  The other young, with sweet seraphic glance. Around went on the Town's satanic dance,  Hunger a-piping while at heart he bled. _Shalom Aleichem_ mournfully each said,  Nor eyed the other straight but looked askance.

Five centres of self-complacent misery were sitting on a cane-seated bench; the sixth person was leaning against the wall with his hands in his pockets. The only other representative of the male sex was eight years old, and had come to have a tooth out; too stolid to feel nervous, he sat sucking peppermints.

arxiv-2201-08754.title: Probing the Degree of Coherence through the Full 1D to 3D crossover
arxiv-2201-08754.creator: R. Shah, T. J. Barrett, A. Colcelli, F. Oručević, A. Trombettoni, P. Krüger
arxiv-2201-08754.description: Abstract We experimentally study a gas of quantum degenerate 87 Rb atoms throughout the full dimensional crossover, from a one-dimensional (1D) system exhibiting phase fluctuations consistent with 1D theory to a three-dimensional (3D) phase-coherent system, thereby smoothly interpolating between these distinct, well-understood regimes.

arxiv-2302-07832.title: Deep Anomaly Detection under Labeling Budget Constraints
arxiv-2302-07832.creator: Aodong Li, Chen Qiu, Marius Kloft, Padhraic Smyth, Stephan Mandt, Maja Rudolph
arxiv-2302-07832.description: Abstract Selecting informative data points for expert feedback can significantly improve the performance of anomaly detection (AD)in various contexts, such as medical diagnostics or fraud detection. In this paper, we determine a set of theoretical conditions under which anomaly scores generalize from labeled queries to unlabeled data.

arxiv-2308-16137.title: LM-Infinite: Zero-Shot Extreme Length Generalization for Large Language Models
arxiv-2308-16137.creator: Chi Han, Qifan Wang, Hao Peng, Wenhan Xiong, Yu Chen, Heng Ji, Sinong Wang
arxiv-2308-16137.description: Abstract Today’s large language models (LLMs) typically train on short text segments (e.g., <4K tokens) due to the quadratic complexity of their Transformer architectures. As a result, their performance suffers drastically on inputs longer than those encountered during training, substantially limiting their applications in real-world tasks involving long contexts such as encoding scientific articles, code repositories, or long dialogues.

arxiv-2311-10775.title: ToolTalk: Evaluating Tool Usage in a Conversational Setting
arxiv-2311-10775.creator: Nicholas Farn and Richard Shin Microsoft Corporation {nifarn,eush}@microsoft.com
arxiv-2311-10775.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have displayed massive improvements in reasoning and decision-making skills and can hold natural conversations with users. Many recent works seek to augment LLM-based assistants with external tools so they can access private or up-to-date information and carry out actions on behalf of users.

arxiv-2312-09367.title: Text-Guided Face Recognition using Multi-Granularity Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning
arxiv-2312-09367.creator: Md Mahedi Hasan, Shoaib Meraj Sami, Nasser Nasrabadi
arxiv-2312-09367.description: Abstract State-of-the-art face recognition (FR) models often experience a significant performance drop when dealing with facial images in surveillance scenarios where images are in low quality and often corrupted with noise. Leveraging facial characteristics, such as freckles, scars, gender, and ethnicity, becomes highly beneficial in improving FR performance in such scenarios.

arxiv-2403-06327.title: Hybrid Soft Electrostatic Metamaterial Gripper for Multi-surface, Multi-object Adaptation Thanks: $*$ Address all correspondence to these authors.
arxiv-2403-06327.creator: Ryo Kanno, Student Member, IEEE, Pham H. Nguyen, Member, IEEE, Joshua Pinskier, Member, IEEE, David Howard, Member, IEEE, Sukho Song, Member, IEEE, Mirko Kovac, Member, IEEE
arxiv-2403-06327.description: Abstract One of the trendsetting themes in soft robotics has been the goal of developing the ultimate universal soft robotic gripper. One that is capable of manipulating items of various shapes, sizes, thicknesses, textures, and weights. All the while still being lightweight and scalable in order to adapt to use cases.

arxiv-2412-06390.title: Edge Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient: efficient continuous control for edge scenarios
arxiv-2412-06390.creator: Alberto Sinigaglia, Niccolò Turcato, Carli Ruggero, Gian Antonio Susto
arxiv-2412-06390.description: Abstract Note to Practitioners Driven by the growing need for efficient computational solutions in automation, this research introduces the Edge Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (EdgeD3), a novel Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithm designed for applications on edge devices with a limited computational budget.

arxiv-2505-15351.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene, Sjoerd Dirksen, Jonathan Dong, Julien Flamant, Mark Iwen, Felix Krahmer, Tristan van Leeuwen, Oleh Melnyk, Andreas Menzel, Allard P. Mosk, Viktor Nikitin, Palina Salanevich, Gerlind Plonka, Matthias Wellershoff. Phase retrieval is an inverse problem that, on one hand, is crucial in many applications across imaging and physics, and, on the other hand, leads to deep research questions in theoretical signal processing and applied harmonic analysis.

arxiv-2506-23209.title: A Hierarchical Slice Attention Network for Appendicitis Classification in 3D CT Scans
arxiv-2506-23209.creator: Chia-Wen Huang, Haw Hwai, Chien-Chang Lee, Pei-Yuan Wu
arxiv-2506-23209.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chia-Wen Huang, Haw Hwai, Chien-Chang Lee, Pei-Yuan Wu. Timely and accurate diagnosis of appendicitis is critical in clinical settings to prevent serious complications. While CT imaging remains the standard diagnostic tool, the growing number of cases can overwhelm radiologists, potentially causing delays. In this paper, we propose a deep learning model that leverages 3D CT scans for appendicitis classification, incorporating Slice Attention mechanisms guided by external 2D datasets to enhance small lesion detection.

arxiv-2510-25181.title: Fed-PELAD: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning for Massive MIMO CSI Feedback with Personalized Encoders and a LoRA-Adapted Shared Decoder The authors are with the School of Information Science and Electronic Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China (e-mail: yxzhou02@163.com, {w69698,
arxiv-2510-25181.creator: Yixiang Zhou, Tong Wu, Meixia Tao, and Jianhua Mo
arxiv-2510-25181.description: Abstract This paper addresses the critical challenges of communication overhead, data heterogeneity, and privacy in deep learning for channel state information (CSI) feedback in massive MIMO systems. To this end, we propose Fed-PELAD, a novel federated learning framework that incorporates personalized encoders and a LoRA-adapted shared decoder.

pmc-10571523.creator: Norio Ushio, Md Nazmul Hasan, Mohammad Arif, Naoki Miura, María Dolores Llobat Bordes, Pablo Jesús Marín-García
pmc-10571523.description: Simple SummaryHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is difficult to distinguish from hepatocellular adenoma (HCA) in dogs, and HCC may develop from HCA, according to recent reports. Therefore, urgent research is needed to establish a reliable biomarker for the early detection of these hepatic diseases. Noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) could be a very useful tool for diagnosing hepatic diseases.

pmc-11508474.title: Assessment of the Impact of Bone Quality and Abutment Configuration on the Fatigue Performance of Dental Implant Systems Using Finite Element Analysis (FEA)
pmc-11508474.creator: Meryem Erdoğdu, Mehmet Gökberkkaan Demirel, Reza Mohammadi, Neslihan Güntekin, Chien-Hung Lee, MacIej Jedliński, Joanna Janiszewska-Olszowska, Marta Mazur

Healthy bone (Hb) and resorbed bone (Rb) were used.

pmc-11514273.title: Community-based nutrition education and counselling provided during pregnancy: effects on knowledge and attitude towards iron-folic acid supplementation
pmc-11514273.creator: Mensur Reshid, Anchamo Anato
pmc-11514273.description: Maternal malnutrition is pervasive throughout the world, notably in sub-Saharan Africa, including Ethiopia. This study examined the effect of community-based iron-folic acid supplementation (IFAS) nutrition education on IFAS knowledge and attitude among pregnant women in urban settings in South Ethiopia.

pmc-11656973.title: Navigating recovery in childhood OCD: a qualitative analysis of barriers and facilitators
pmc-11656973.creator: Lakshmi Sravanti, Rajendra Kiragasur Madegowda, Arul Jayendra Pradeep Velusamy, John Vijay Sagar Kommu, Satish Chandra Girimaji, Shekhar Seshadri
pmc-11656973.description: ObjectiveThe objective is to examine barriers and facilitators to recovery in children and adolescents with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) using a qualitative approach.MethodsTen semi-structured interviews were conducted, audio-recorded, and analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings were validated through investigator triangulation, peer validation and member check.

pmc-12734119.title: One Sport or Many? Comparing the Effects of Athletics and Multiactivity Training on Motor Competence in 6–10-Year-Olds—A Case Study
pmc-12734119.creator: Nataniel Lopes, Miguel Jacinto, Diogo Monteiro, Rui Matos, Sérgio J Ibáñez, Giuseppe Musumeci
pmc-12734119.description: Background: Motor competence (MC) is defined as the ability to perform a wide range of motor skills with proficiency and control. The present quasi-experimental study design examines the impact of two structured intervention programs on MC in children who practiced athletics at the same club, aged 6 to 10 years, implemented over 12 weeks.

pmc-12949953.title: Menopausal hormone therapy and risk of neuropsychiatric disease: a drug target Mendelian randomisation study
pmc-12949953.creator: Louise S Schindler, Dipender Gill, Hannah Oppenheimer, Claudia Barth, Ole A Andreassen, Bogdan Draganski, Lars T Westlye, Anya Topiwala, Ann-Marie G de Lange
pmc-12949953.description: Evidence on whether menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) affects neurological or psychiatric disease is conflicting. As MHT acts by binding to oestrogen receptors (ERα and ERβ), we used drug-target Mendelian randomisation (MR) to test whether perturbing these targets alters the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), brain structure, depression, or anxiety.

pmc-13101127.title: Single cell protein profiling of focal cortical dysplasia in a patient requiring multiple resections
pmc-13101127.creator: Nada A. Elsayed, Robert P. Naftel, Bret C. Mobley, Allyson L. Alexander, Angus M. Toland, Asa A. Brockman, Jonathan M. Irish, Rebecca A. Ihrie, Kevin C. Ess
pmc-13101127.description: Epilepsy affects millions worldwide with many failing to respond to standard treatments. Drug-refractory epilepsy requiring surgical intervention often presents due to developmental aberrations, such as focal cortical dysplasia (FCD). In FCD type II, somatic mutations in the mTOR pathway allow excessive activation of the mTOR kinase, causing unregulated cell growth and differentiation.

pmc-13700049.title: Doing More With Less in Coronary Intervention
pmc-13700049.creator: Abuduwufuer Yidilisi, Jun Jiang
pmc-13700049.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Corresponding Author Functional and intravascular imaging assessments offer distinct yet complementary perspectives in coronary intervention, integrating physiological and anatomical information to guide clinical decision-making. Functional metrics, such as fractional flow reserve (FFR), are pivotal in determining “whether intervention is necessary,” whereas morphologic assessments via intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or optical coherence tomography (OCT) guide “how to optimize the intervention” and identify vulnerable plaques.
